transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22 | Start: 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~54m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Vertex VP Product), Miguel Torres (Vertex Head of ML), Jason Reed (Vertex Security), Anita Kumar (PM)

Summary (auto):
POC timeline & milestones for Vertex Health to validate Redwood inference for clinical summarization. Focus on success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), workload sizing, benchmark plan, security/access flow, and exec readout.

Topics: kickoff, access setup, benchmark plan, mid-point review, exec readout, security controls

Action items (captured): see metadata above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we'll give a quick agenda — confirm success criteria, outline a 4-week POC timeline with key milestones, plus access and security tasks. Sound good?
[00:12] Sara Patel: Yeah, that works for us. We're primarily focused on clinical note summarization and triage routing, so performance and privacy are top of mind.
[00:20] Miguel Torres: Yep, and we want to see both latency and accuracy compared to our current pipeline. Also want to understand cost implications.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks. Quick intro — I'm Liam, SE at Redwood, I'll own the benchmark plan and perf scripts. Priya's on the infra side for private deployment questions.
[00:37] Priya Rao: Hi all.
[00:39] Jason Reed: Jason from security — I'll need to review SOC2 and KMS details.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Quick qualification: what's your current stack for inference? Miguel?
[00:49] Miguel Torres: We're running a mix — some CPU-based microservices on-prem and a small GPU cluster in GCP for heavy models. Throughput is variable; typical peak is around 200 requests per minute for summarization during business hours, spiking to maybe 600 during overnight batch windows. Latency SLA target is sub 300ms for user-facing summarization flows, but we'd like to tighten that.
[01:10] Anita Kumar: Our timelines — product wants a decision by end of August for Q4 rollout planning. So a 4-week POC in August would fit.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Good — that's aligned. Proposed POC scope: 4 weeks. Week 0: kickoff + access setup. Week 1-2: benchmarks and tuning (we'll run latency/throughput tests, accuracy evals). Week 3: mid-point review and tuning. Week 4: exec readout and handoff.
[01:34] Sara Patel: Sounds right. For success criteria, what would you recommend we validate?
[01:39] Liam O'Connor: We usually propose three buckets: performance (median and tail latencies, 95/99p), accuracy (ROUGE/F1 or domain-specific labels), and cost (estimate per 1M tokens or per request). For this workload, maybe: median token latency <150ms, 95p request latency <300ms, accuracy drop <5% from your baseline, and cost target under X — we'll put numbers in BOM.
[02:02] Miguel Torres: The <5% accuracy drop is reasonable; our baseline ROUGE is about 0.62 for summaries. Cost target — we'll give a threshold offline.
[02:11] Jason Reed: On security, we need SOC2, SAML SSO for the console, audit logs, and KMS integration. If we do private deployment, VPC peering and HSM/KMS key control are must-haves.
[02:26] Priya Rao: We support both hosted and private; for a first POC we can do a private tenant with customer-managed VPC connections or a fully hosted POC with encrypted-at-rest and strict retention. We'll send a short matrix of tradeoffs.
[02:39] Maya Chen: Noted. Tradeoff conversation: hosted is fastest to start, but dedicated/private gives more control and often lower tail latency. There's often a throughput vs cost tradeoff if you pick dedicated GPUs.
[02:52] Anita Kumar: We might start hosted to move fast, then switch to dedicated if latency tails are an issue.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: That approach works. For our benchmarks, we'll plan both modes — run a hosted baseline and then repeat on a dedicated pool config that we recommend. We'll include quantization variants and batching profiles.
[03:10] Sara Patel: How will you simulate our workload? We have bursts and also long context notes.
[03:16] Liam O'Connor: We'll need a sample corpus — maybe 2000 anonymized notes that reflect typical length distribution. If you can provide a histogram of sequence lengths and a few real samples (PII redacted), we'll craft the QPS profile: steady-state at 100 QPS per instance, spikes to 500/1000 depending on the test.
[03:34] Miguel Torres: We can do that. We'll prepare a small scrubbed dataset by Aug 1.
[03:40] Maya Chen: Great. Benchmarks: we'll measure median, 95th, 99th latencies, and end-to-end throughput with varying batch sizes. We'll also capture token-level costs and KV cache hit rates — plz note sometimes transcripts show K V cache.
[03:56] Priya Rao: Regarding KV cache, for long context we should enable prefix caching where possible to reduce recomputation. We'll include cache policy suggestions.
[04:06] Jason Reed: On encryption, KMS integration is mandatory for private. For hosted we'd prefer CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) if available. Also need egress controls and audit logs retention settings.
[04:18] Maya Chen: We'll attach our security packet — SOC2 report, SAML guides, KMS/CMEK options, and a sample network diagram for VPC peering.
[04:26] Sara Patel: Can you also include a sample BOM? CPU/GPU counts, anticipated throughput, and cost buckets?
[04:32] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send a BOM and an estimated cost model.
[04:36] Anita Kumar: Timeline specifics — can we schedule kickoff the week of Aug 4th? We have a blocked window Aug 5th 10am PT.
[04:44] Maya Chen: Aug 5th 10am PT works from our side. We'll set that as the kickoff.
[04:48] Liam O'Connor: For the kickoff we'll request that Jason or your infra lead provide the VPC contact and any access tickets. Also privileged accounts for the test environment.
[04:58] Jason Reed: I'll assign an infra engineer and pass contact info by 7/28.
[05:02] Miguel Torres: For benchmarks, what's the expected deliverable after week 2? A runbook plus perf docs?
[05:09] Liam O'Connor: Deliverables: benchmark results (raw logs and summary), a tuning guide with recommended quantization and batching configs, and a small dashboard with latency/cost breakdown by route. We'll present at the mid-point review and iterate.
[05:21] Priya Rao: We'll also include a suggested model variant list — e.g., llama-based 13B quantized, 7B float, etc. We'll map them to cost/latency profiles.
[05:30] Sara Patel: Any blockers we should know about?
[05:33] Maya Chen: The main dependencies are the scrubbed dataset, infra contact for VPC/KMS, and an agreed success criteria doc. If any of those slip we may need to extend the POC by a week.
[05:44] Anita Kumar: Understood. We'll prioritize dataset and infra contact.
[05:49] Miguel Torres: One question — for accuracy evals, can you support our custom metrics? We have a triage accuracy label set that's fairly specific.
[05:57] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. We'll add hooks in the eval harness for your labels; we'll need a small truth set.
[06:03] Jason Reed: Any legal or procurement items to start? We have an NDA in place. For the POC, do you require a PO?
[06:10] Maya Chen: No PO for the short POC normally; we'll use a trial agreement. For enterprise options we'll move to SOW/PO. We'll share the trial agreement and the security docs after the call.
[06:20] Sara Patel: Good. For the exec readout, our VP Eng wants a 15-20 minute summary plus a demo. Can Redwood present?
[06:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll prepare an exec slide pack and a short demo. We'll aim for week of Aug 25 for exec readout. Anita will coordinate the exact slot.
[06:36] Anita Kumar: I'll pick a time and get back by Aug 8th.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Great. Recap: Kickoff Aug 5th, Vertex to provide scrubbed dataset by Aug 1, Jason to provide infra contacts by Jul 28, Redwood to send BOM, security docs, and benchmark plan by Jul 25, Redwood SE to deliver perf scripts by Jul 29, mid-point review week of Aug 12, exec readout week of Aug 25.
[06:58] Miguel Torres: That aligns.
[07:00] Sara Patel: Thanks everyone.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with an email containing links and attachments.
[07:06] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: moderate ASR errors, some product names may be slightly off.
